questions.html: What is the time complexity of the ‘delete( )’ operation in a singly linked list?
questions.solution:
(c)
In a singly linked list, the ‘delete( )’ operation (removing a node from the list) has a time complexity of Ο(n). This is because in the worst case, you may need to traverse the entire list to find the node to be deleted.

questions.html:
Below of the following Python code?
list_a = [1, 2, 3]
list_b = [4, 5, 6]
result_list = list_a * 2 + list_b
print(result_list)
What will be sum of items when output is printed?
questions.solution:
27
• The ‘*’ operator duplicates the elements of a list. In this code, ‘list_a * 2’ duplicates the elements of ‘list_a’, resulting in ‘[1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3]’.
• Then, ‘list_a * 2 + list_b’ concatenates this duplicated list with ‘list_b’, resulting in ‘[1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]’.
